{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2020}}
'''Kayo Inaba''' is a professor at [[Kyoto University]] where she heads the Graduate School of Biostudies. She is also the Vice-President for Gender Equality and the Director of the Centre for Women Researchers.

Inaho is known for her work on [[dendritic cells]] and she won the Asia pacific [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|UNESCO Awards for Women in Science]] in 2014. She has shown the importance of dendritic cells to the [[immune system]] and how they can live outside of the body.<ref name=dis>[http://discov-her.com/en/article/treating-cells-outside-the-human-body Treating cells outside the human body] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160625130011/http://discov-her.com/en/article/treating-cells-outside-the-human-body |date=2016-06-25 }}, Discov-ger.com, Retrieved 30 July 2015</ref>

==Life==
Inaba graduated from the [[Kyoto University]] with a Ph.D. in 1978.
From  1982 until 2011, She was visiting faculty member in [[Ralph Steinman]]’s lab.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adjunct faculty member Kayo Inaba receives L'Oréal-UNESCO Women in Science award|url=http://newswire.rockefeller.edu/2014/03/03/adjunct-faculty-member-kayo-inaba-receives-loreal-unesco-women-in-science-award/|publisher=Rockefeller University|accessdate=11 August 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907025432/http://newswire.rockefeller.edu/2014/03/03/adjunct-faculty-member-kayo-inaba-receives-loreal-unesco-women-in-science-award/|archivedate=7 September 2015}}</ref>
She is executive vice-president for gender equality, international affairs, public relations, and director of the International Strategy Office at Kyoto University.<ref>[https://www.kyoto-u.ac.jp/en/about/profile/executive President, Executive Vice-Presidents, and Vice-Presidents on Kyoto university website]</ref>
Inaba was the first female associate professor in the science department at Kyoto University.<ref name=dis/> 
Inaba is on the board of the Japanese Society for Immunology.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064815/http://www.hasumi-foundation.org/bio021.html Dr Inaba]}}, Hasumi Foundation, Retrieved 30 July 2015</ref>

In 2024, she was designated a [[Person of Cultural Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUE216G80R21C24A0000000/|title= ちばてつや氏ら7人に文化勲章 功労者に青木功氏ら|access-date= 25 October 2024|work= The Nikkei|date= 25 October 2024}}</ref>
